newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea probes associate of president's son.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea probes associate of president's son.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors began questioning a key associate of President Kim Young-sam's son to find out if the younger Kim accepted kickbacks in return for influence, state radio said on Sunday.

Korea Broadcasting Sytem (KBS) said Lee Song-ho, suspected of managing slush funds for Kim Hyun-chul and possessing information about alleged influence-peddling, voluntarily appeared before the prosecutors office on Sunday.

KBS said state prosecutors have begun probing government projects and had confirmed that a local construction company deposited more than one billion won ($1.12 million) in a bank account suspected of being opened on behalf of Kim Hyun-chul.
"The prosecution is focusing its probe on whether the money was a kickback in connection with a large government construction project," KBS said.

Kim Hyun-chul is under investigation over allegations that he meddled in state affairs, kept part of unspent funds from his father's election campaign in 1992, and played a role in a loans-for-kickbacks scandal involving failed Hanbo Steel Co.
Lee, former president of Dae Ho Construction Co, arrived in Seoul on Sunday. He had gone to the United States after allegations against the younger Kim first came to light.

The leading Chosun Ilbo newspaper said prosecutors had investigated Dae Ho Construction, which had secured more than 10 billion won worth of government orders since 1993 when President Kim took office.

The daily said prosecutors believed construction units of five to six business conglomerates, or chaebol, also deposited hundreds of millions of won to accounts controlled by associates of Kim Hyun-chul.
Prosecution officials were not available for comment on Sunday.

Last week, a prosecution spokesman said prosecutors could not find any link between Kim Hyun-chul and the Hanbo scandal but had secured enough evidence to charge him this month for "irregularities unrelated to Hanbo".
The younger Kim has denied any links with Hanbo Steel, which collapsed in January revealing a web of corrupt alliances between politicians, businessmen and bankers.

Prosecutors have said they have secured evidence that executives of several companies looked after large sums of money linked to Kim Hyun-chul's associates, but were unable to confirm the sources of the funds.
It said investigators tried to establish if the money was paid after the companies won government projects.
Chosun Ilbo said prosecutors would summon Kim Hyun-chul this week and were likely to take legal action before May 20.

The main opposition National Congress for New Politics has alleged Kim Hyun-chul, who helped engineer his father's 1992 election victory, pressured banks to keep loans rolling into Hanbo Steel in return for a donation worth tens of billions of won to help finance the 1992 campaign. (US$1 = 894 won)
